title: Cap. X Arg. X: elect/non-elect divide arises from God’s diverse decrees of preparing and giving—not from human operations about commonly offered grace; Arminius intolerable
pass_a_gloss: From all which it is manifest that The discrimination of elect and non-elect, of believing and not-believing, of persevering and not-persevering arises not from antecedent and discrete operations of human wills about grace commonly offered, but from antecedent and diverse decrees and operations of God, in decreeing, preparing, and giving unto one what he has not decreed, nor prepared, nor given unto the other. Intolerable therefore is Arminius’s sentence, which refers unto God a certain common preparation and offer of grace, but refers unto the free will of singular men, stirred by this common grace, the very discrimination of believers and non-believers, elect and non-elect.
pass_b_english: From all this it is plain: the divide of elect and non-elect, believers and unbelievers, those who persevere and those who do not, does not arise from prior, distinct human-will operations about commonly offered grace, but from God’s prior, diverse decrees and workings—decreeing, preparing, and giving to one what he neither decreed nor prepared nor gave to the other. So Arminius’s view is intolerable: it credits God with a common preparation and offer of grace, but credits each person’s free will, stirred by that common grace, with the very discrimination of believers and unbelievers, elect and non-elect.
source_text: Ex quibus omnibus manifestum est, Discrimen electorum et non-electorum, credentium et non-credentium, perseverantium et non-perseverantium oriri non ex antecedaneis et discretis humanarum voluntatum circa gratiam communiter oblatam operationibus, sed ex antecedaneis et diversis Dei decretis et operationibus, in decernendo, praeparando et donando uni quod non decrevit, neque praeparavit neque donavit alteri. Intoleranda est igitur Arminii sententia, quae ad Deum refert communem quandam gratiae praeparationem et oblationem, ad singulorum autem hominum liberum arbitrium hac communi gratia excitatum refert ipsam discriminationem credentium et non-credentium, electorum et non-electorum.
